current.stdout:
Usage:
  opf convert <input|-> <output|-> [--from <format>] [--to <format>] [--force] [--fail-on <level>] [format flags]

Convert a deck or a .pptx to another form: a deck form, PDF, PPTX, PNG or SVG per slide, a .zip of slides, or stdout.

Formats. Input: .json, .opf.yaml/.yaml/.yml, .opf.md and a plain .md (OPF Markdown, an outline included), .pptx, or -
(stdin: --from json|yaml|md|pptx, else text starting with { or [ is JSON). Output: .json, .opf.yaml/.yml, .opf.md, .pdf, .pptx,
.png and .svg (one file per slide beside the output: slides/deck.png gives slides/deck-1.png, padded to the largest slide
number written, so deck-01.png from ten slides; one selected slide is written to the output itself; {n} in the output is the
slide number: slides/slide-{n}.png always numbers its files, even for one slide, and with --slides 2,5 writes slide-2.png and
slide-5.png; any other {key}, and {n} in a single-file output, is exit 2), .zip (the slides as png, or svg with --to svg;
entries named like slides/deck.png's files), or - (stdout: --to json|yaml|md|pdf|pptx|png|svg|zip; png and svg need exactly
one slide). --to that disagrees with the output's extension is refused.

Flags, each only where its format is involved (otherwise exit 2):
  Markdown input   --split <auto|rules|headings>  slides at --- lines, and in an outline with none at # headings (auto, the default)
                   --title <text>                 the deck name unless the front matter sets one
  YAML input       --aliases                      expand anchors, aliases and merge keys (at most 100)
  .pptx input      --signals <file>               also write the per-shape layout and style signals as JSON
  YAML output      --schema-comment               start with the yaml-language-server $schema line
  Markdown output  --drop-unsupported             leave out what the dialect has no syntax for (listed as loss) instead of
                                                  embedding it as YAML in a fence
  pdf, png, svg    --slides <1,3-5>  --include-hidden
  pdf, png, svg,   --date <YYYY-MM-DD>  --fonts <dir>... (.ttf and .otf files)  --asset-dir <dir>
  and pptx         --paginate                     split every slide that overflows, as opf paginate does. Without it a slide
                                                  of sibling blocks of one kind (eight timelines) that overflows continues on
                                                  further slides between whole blocks (slide-continued, report continued)
                   --keep-slides                  draw every slide as written, also one that overflows
  pptx             --charts <auto|native|picture>  --images <compatible|preserve>  --provenance <full|references-only|none>
                   --diagrams <shapes|picture>    shapes (the default): native shapes, text and connectors for the diagram
                                                  families that passed their comparison with the preview in PowerPoint; the
                                                  others stay pictures (diagram-shapes-unavailable). picture: each diagram one
                                                  SVG picture
                   --body-text <measured|native>  measured (the default): every wrapped line is its own text box, laid out as the
                                                  preview draws it. native: opt in to whole paragraphs, a wrapped title as the
                                                  Title placeholder and a text or list as one body, so PowerPoint and Keynote
                                                  re-wrap edited text; what it cannot carry stays measured (native-body-fallback)
                   --smart-art <live|shapes>      a pyramid, matrix or cycle layout: live (the default) writes live SmartArt where
                                                  PowerPoint draws it as the preview does, else native shapes (smartart-
                                                  unavailable says why); shapes writes native shapes always
                   --slide-numbers <static|live>  a footer like "{{slide.number}} / {{deck.slideCount}}": live (the default)
                                                  keeps the slide-number field, so PowerPoint renumbers it, but Keynote shows it
                                                  as the digit alone; static writes the number as fixed text, so Keynote shows
                                                  the words too. A bare {{slide.number}} stays a live field either way
                   --typefaces <selected|safe>    selected (the default): the families the deck chose; a viewer without one
                                                  substitutes another font (typeface-not-office-safe names them). safe: write
                                                  each Latin text family as Arial, Georgia, Courier New or Times New Roman,
                                                  on every Windows and macOS machine, and lay the text out with it, so every
                                                  viewer breaks lines where the file does (typeface-replaced)
                   --as <native|images>           native (the default): editable shapes, text and charts. images: a
                                                  fidelity fallback, each slide one full-bleed PNG picture drawn like the
                                                  preview (--scale, default 2), with its speaker notes and its text as the
                                                  picture's alt text; it needs no fonts and has no editable text
  png, raster pdf, --scale <0.1-8>                1 draws the 1280 x 720 reference slide at 1280 x 720 pixels
  pptx --as images
  pdf              --raster                       each page a picture instead of selectable vector text
  svg              --text <fonts|system|paths>    embed the faces the slide uses (fonts), none (system), or draw outlines (paths)

The deck is checked (format and references) first; findings at or above --fail-on (default error) write nothing (exit 1). An
existing output needs --force. Drawing never loads system fonts and never fetches URLs; images resolve next to the input unless
--asset-dir. PDF, PNG, SVG and PPTX need the optional @openpresentation/opf-render (and opf-pptx for .pptx); a missing one is
exit 2 with the one command that installs it (see opf doctor). The report: { command, ok, input, outputs: [{ file, sha256,
bytes, mediaType }], findings, counts, format, ... }, on stderr when the output is stdout.

Examples:
  opf convert deck.opf.md slides/deck.png --slides 1,3-5 --scale 2
  opf convert deck.opf.md "slides/slide-{n}.png"
  opf convert deck.pptx deck.opf.md --signals signals.json
  opf convert outline.md deck.opf.yaml
  opf convert deck.opf.json deck.opf.yaml --schema-comment
  opf convert deck.opf.json deck.pptx --typefaces safe
  opf convert deck.opf.json deck.pptx --as images
  opf convert deck.opf.md - --to pdf > deck.pdf
